Description: [New] The stray time-field icon is removed from the app parameter time placeholder
Pre-requisite Data: Param1 = the application parameter screen containing the payment plan time parameter; Time1 = that time field while it is empty and showing only its placeholder text.
Test Data: Open Param1 and look at the empty time field Time1.
Expected Output: The empty time field shows clean placeholder text only. The old clock/time icon that used to sit inside the placeholder is removed (or corrected), so nothing is clipped, overlapped or half-drawn inside the field.
Verification Step: 1. Open Param1 and locate Time1 with no value entered. 2. Assert the placeholder text is fully readable from its first to its last character. 3. Assert no stray or clipped icon is drawn inside the field over the placeholder. 4. Assert any icon that is intentionally kept sits neatly at the field edge without overlapping the text. 5. Zoom the browser in and out and assert the field stays clean at each zoom level. 6. Check the field on a narrow window width and assert the placeholder still does not collide with an icon.

Description: [New] The time parameter still accepts, validates and saves a time value after the placeholder icon change
Pre-requisite Data: Param1 = the application parameter screen; Time1 = the payment plan time parameter field; T1 = a valid time value; T2 = an invalid time entry.
Test Data: Enter T1 and then T2 into Time1 and save Param1.
Expected Output: The icon cleanup is cosmetic only: the time field still opens its picker (if provided), accepts a valid time, rejects an invalid one, and persists the saved value across a reload.
Verification Step: 1. Open Param1 and click into Time1. 2. Assert the time picker opens if one is provided, or that manual typing is allowed. 3. Enter T1 and assert it is accepted and displayed in the expected format. 4. Save and reload Param1; assert Time1 still shows T1. 5. Clear the field, enter T2 and assert the invalid entry is rejected with a clear message. 6. Assert the placeholder returns cleanly when the field is cleared, with no icon artefact. 7. Confirm no console/script error is raised while interacting with the field.

Description: [New] Client setting 'Show Agreement on Payment Plan' exists and offers exactly three values
Pre-requisite Data: Cfg1 = the client setting screen holding 'Show Agreement on Payment Plan'; the three intended values are 'Yes & Keep it mandatory', 'Yes but not mandatory' and 'No'.
Test Data: Open Cfg1 and open the 'Show Agreement on Payment Plan' dropdown.
Expected Output: The setting is present and its dropdown lists exactly three options - 'Yes & Keep it mandatory', 'Yes but not mandatory' and 'No' - with the labels spelled as specified and no extra or duplicate entry.
Verification Step: 1. Open Cfg1 and locate the setting named 'Show Agreement on Payment Plan'. 2. Assert the setting is displayed with that exact label. 3. Open its dropdown and count the options; assert there are exactly three. 4. Assert the first option reads 'Yes & Keep it mandatory'. 5. Assert the second option reads 'Yes but not mandatory'. 6. Assert the third option reads 'No'. 7. Assert no blank, duplicate or legacy option is listed.

Description: [New] The 'Show Agreement on Payment Plan' selection is saved and persists across reload and re-login
Pre-requisite Data: Cfg1 = the client setting screen; Opt1, Opt2 = two different values of 'Show Agreement on Payment Plan'; User1 = a user with rights to change client settings.
Test Data: As User1 select Opt1 in Cfg1 and save, reload, then change to Opt2 and save.
Expected Output: The chosen value is stored at client level: it is still selected after a page reload and after logging out and in again, and changing it to another value replaces the old one cleanly.
Verification Step: 1. Log in as User1 and open Cfg1. 2. Note the value shown when the setting is first opened on an untouched client. 3. Select Opt1 and Save; assert a success confirmation is shown. 4. Reload Cfg1 and assert Opt1 is still selected. 5. Log out, log in again and reopen Cfg1; assert Opt1 is still selected. 6. Change the value to Opt2 and Save; reload and assert Opt2 is selected and Opt1 is no longer stored. 7. Confirm the change is visible to a second user of the same client.

Description: [New] 'Show Agreement on Payment Plan' is a fixed dropdown - it cannot be left blank or free-typed
Pre-requisite Data: Cfg1 = the client setting screen; Opt1 = any valid value of 'Show Agreement on Payment Plan'; Txt1 = an arbitrary text string that is not one of the three allowed values.
Test Data: Attempt to clear the setting and to type Txt1 into it, then save Cfg1.
Expected Output: The control behaves as a closed list: the user cannot type a free value, cannot save a blank value, and only one of the three defined options can ever be stored.
Verification Step: 1. Open Cfg1 and focus the 'Show Agreement on Payment Plan' control. 2. Try to type Txt1 directly into it and assert the text is not accepted as a value. 3. Try to clear the selection entirely and Save; assert either the save is blocked or the control falls back to a valid option, never to blank. 4. Select Opt1 and Save; assert it stores successfully. 5. Reopen the dropdown and assert it still lists only the three defined options. 6. Confirm the stored value read back after reload is exactly one of the three allowed labels.

Description: [New] A fresh database already carries the default letter templates for every payment-plan reminder and notification event
Pre-requisite Data: DB1 = a freshly created database where no one has manually added letter templates; Ev1 = the list of payment-plan events that need a default template (payment successful, payment failed, payment plan setup, payment plan status change, payment due reminder, card expiry reminder, payment plan agreement).
Test Data: Open the letter template list in DB1 and look for a default template for each event in Ev1.
Expected Output: Because the default templates are applied to all databases by default, DB1 already contains one ready-to-use default template for each event in Ev1 without any manual import.
Verification Step: 1. Open the letter/template setup in DB1. 2. Filter or search for payment-plan related templates. 3. For each event in Ev1, assert a default template exists. 4. Open one default template and assert it has real content rather than an empty shell. 5. Assert each template is active and available for selection. 6. Assert no event in Ev1 is left without a template. 7. Confirm the templates were present without any manual creation step being performed in DB1.

Description: [New] Each payment-plan event's default letter template is selectable from the notification/reminder setup dropdown
Pre-requisite Data: Pref1 = the Notification & Reminder Preference setup for payment plans; Ev1 = a payment-plan event such as payment due or card expiry; Tpl1 = the default letter template shipped for Ev1.
Test Data: Open Pref1, pick the event Ev1 and open its template dropdown.
Expected Output: The default template Tpl1 for the event is listed in the template dropdown and can be selected and saved, so the clinic can go live without authoring its own template first.
Verification Step: 1. Open Pref1 and select the payment plan event Ev1. 2. Open the Email template dropdown and assert Tpl1 is listed. 3. Open the Text/SMS template dropdown and assert its shipped default is listed too. 4. Select Tpl1 and Save. 5. Reopen Pref1 and assert the selection persisted. 6. Assert the preview (if available) renders the default template content. 7. Repeat for a second event in the payment-plan event list and assert its default is likewise selectable.

Description: [New] The default payment-plan templates are applied to every database, not just one
Pre-requisite Data: DB1, DB2 = two different databases/clients of the product; Ev1 = the payment-plan reminder and notification event list.
Test Data: Check the payment-plan default letter templates in DB1 and then in DB2.
Expected Output: Both databases carry the same set of default templates for the payment-plan events, proving the defaults were rolled out to all databases rather than seeded in one only.
Verification Step: 1. Open the letter template setup in DB1 and list the payment-plan default templates. 2. Record which events in Ev1 are covered. 3. Switch to DB2 and open its letter template setup. 4. Assert DB2 covers the same events in Ev1. 5. Compare one default template's body in DB1 and DB2 and assert the shipped content matches. 6. Assert neither database is missing a template for any event. 7. Confirm a template edited locally in DB1 does not change the DB2 copy.

Description: [New] Payment plan screens and setups open for a client that does not have OpenEdge configured
Pre-requisite Data: Client1 = a client/database where OpenEdge is NOT configured; User1 = a user of Client1 with payment plan grants; Setup1 = the Recurring Payment Plan Setup window; Track1 = the plan-level tracking worklist.
Test Data: Log in to Client1 as User1 and open the payment plan menu entries.
Expected Output: All payment plan screens and setups are available to Client1 even without OpenEdge: the menu entries are present and both Setup1 and Track1 open normally. Only the payment method side is restricted, not the screens themselves.
Verification Step: 1. Log in to Client1 as User1. 2. Assert the payment plan menu entries are visible and enabled. 3. Open Setup1 and assert the window loads with its list and form. 4. Open Track1 and assert the worklist loads. 5. Open a patient's payment plan screen and assert it opens. 6. Assert no message is shown claiming the feature requires OpenEdge. 7. Confirm no screen is blank, blocked or error-ed because OpenEdge is absent.

Description: [New] Plan templates can be created, edited and saved on a non-OpenEdge client exactly as on a configured client
Pre-requisite Data: Client1 = a client without OpenEdge configured; Client2 = a client with OpenEdge configured; Setup1 = the Recurring Payment Plan Setup window; Code1 = a new unique plan code.
Test Data: Create and edit a template with plan code Code1 in Setup1 on Client1, then compare the setup form against Client2.
Expected Output: Template creation, editing, activation/deactivation and deletion all work on the non-OpenEdge client, and the setup form offers the same fields as on the OpenEdge client, because setup is gateway-independent.
Verification Step: 1. Log in to Client1 and open Setup1. 2. Create a template with Code1, a description, an amount and a Due On rule; Save. 3. Assert the template saves and appears in the left list. 4. Edit the amount and Save again; assert the change persists. 5. Mark the template inactive and assert it moves to the inactive group. 6. Open Setup1 on Client2 and compare the visible fields; assert the two forms expose the same fields. 7. Confirm nothing in Setup1 is greyed out on Client1 purely because OpenEdge is missing.

Description: [New] FLOW - a non-OpenEdge client sets up a template and uses it on a patient plan, with only the payment method restricted
Pre-requisite Data: Client1 = a client without OpenEdge configured; Setup1 = the Recurring Payment Plan Setup window; Code1 = a new plan code created in Setup1; Pat1 = a patient of Client1.
Test Data: On Client1 create a template under Code1, then build a payment plan for Pat1 from it.
Expected Output: The whole setup-to-plan path works without OpenEdge: the template saves, it is selectable on the patient plan, and the plan can be created and saved. Only the card/payment method area is unavailable or greyed out for this client.
Verification Step: 1. Log in to Client1 and open Setup1. 2. Create and save a template under Code1. 3. Open Pat1's payment plan screen. 4. Assert Code1 is selectable in the Plan Code dropdown and its defaults populate. 5. Assert the payment method / card area is greyed out or unavailable for this client. 6. Complete and save the plan with the remaining fields. 7. Assert the plan saves and appears in the plan-level tracking worklist. 8. Confirm no OpenEdge error is raised at any step.
